hints: Focus on what causes the small M+1 peak in a mass spectrum, it is mainly the natural abundance of carbon-13.
A ratio of 4 to 91 is about 4.4%, and with about 1.1% contribution per carbon atom, this points to a molecule with four carbon atoms.
Now use the oxidation test to decide between the four-carbon choices, remembering only aldehydes and primary alcohols can be heated with acidified dichromate to give a carboxylic acid.
walkthrough:
**Use the M+1 peak to count carbons**

Think of the M+1 peak as counting $^{13}\text{C}$ atoms. Each carbon adds about 1.1% to the height of M+1 relative to M+.

Calculation rule:
$$\text{number of C atoms} \approx \frac{\text{height of M+1}}{\text{height of M+}} \times \frac{100}{1.1}$$

**Apply the numbers from J**

Here the ratio is 4 to 91, so the percentage is very friendly to calculate.

$$\frac{4}{91} \times 100 \approx 4.4\%$$
$$\text{number of C} \approx \frac{4.4}{1.1} = 4$$
So compound J must contain 4 carbon atoms.

**Use oxidation to identify the functional group**

Heating with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is strong oxidation. It turns a primary alcohol into an aldehyde then a carboxylic acid, and an aldehyde straight into a carboxylic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
Ketones resist this oxidation and nitriles do not react this way.

**Match both clues to the list**

Only a four-carbon molecule that can be oxidised to an acid fits. That is butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, which oxidises to butanoic acid.

options.A: Butanal is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ with 4 carbons, giving an M+1 to M+ ratio of about 4.4%, matching 4:91. As an aldehyde it is oxidised by heated acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ to butanoic acid, a carboxylic acid.
options.B: Butanone also has 4 carbons so it fits the mass spectrum clue, but as a ketone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) it is not oxidised by acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ to a carboxylic acid. Students who only use the carbon count often pick this trap.
options.C: Propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) is a primary alcohol so it does oxidise to a carboxylic acid, but it has only 3 carbons. Its M+1 ratio would be about 3.3%, not 4.4%, so it fails the mass spectrum test.
options.D: Propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$) has only 3 carbons and its nitrile group ($-\text{CN}$) is not oxidised to a carboxylic acid by acidified dichromate. It fails both the carbon count and the functional group test.
